models.solution: A solution in the catalogue, of type chat (external bot, endpoint, theme, welcome text, starter prompts, feedback toggle) or embedded (public HTTPS iframe URL, allow fullscreen), with identity, category, and status with reason.
models.category: An ordered grouping of solutions. One category per solution. Solutions without one show under Other.
models.chatTheme: Styling for the chat surface: header color, bubble colors, radius, font, placeholder. The tenant branding is the undeletable default.
models.favorite: A member's pinned solution with a position.
models.recent: A solution the member opened recently, with the opened time.
models.conversation: The member's single current conversation with one solution: the streamed messages of this session only. Genie stores only a session handle; `resumed` is true when the viewer reopened an existing bot-side conversation, and earlier messages are not shown.
models.accessGrant: Effective access to a solution: a role assignment with the solutions:use permission, scoped to the solution or tenant-wide, direct or via a group.
models.viewer: The signed-in person with the permission keys they hold. solutions:admin unlocks the admin views. The sample viewer is a member (Alex Morgan); admin screens are previewed as Priya Nair.
models.approvedFont: A font a chat theme may pick, by id and label. The list is fixed by the platform.
models.person: A person summary for the Access overview picker: name, email, and group names used to resolve grants via groups.
models.chatEnabled: Deployment flag: false when GENIE_CHAT_API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is empty and chat streaming is off (DEC-30).

relationships: solution belongs to zero or one category and to one chatTheme (null means the tenant branding default)
favorite and recent belong to the viewer and to one solution
conversation belongs to the viewer and one solution
accessGrant points at one solution (or all, when scope is tenant) and at a person or group
solution.apiEndpoint is a public HTTPS URL entered per solution; there is no tenant-level list

messages.text: Triage this claim: 54F, day surgery for cataract, invoice SGD 4,200, discharge letter attached, no pre-authorisation form.

messages.reasoning: Elective procedure, amount above the day-surgery threshold, pre-authorisation missing. Routine urgency; list the missing documents.
messages.text:
**Urgency: Routine.**

Cataract day surgery is an elective procedure, so this claim does not need same-day review.

**Missing documents**

1. Pre-authorisation form (required for day surgery above SGD 3,000)
2. Itemised hospital bill

**Suggested next step:** request both from the policyholder before assigning a reviewer.
Is the pre-authorisation form still required if the surgery was an emergency?

No. For emergency admissions the pre-authorisation form is waived, but the claim must include the emergency department note showing the admission time. Cataract surgery is almost never an emergency, so in this case the form is still required.
Show me the triage decision as a flow.

messages.reasoning: A small decision flow: elective versus emergency, then the amount threshold, then the missing-document check.
messages.text:
Here is the decision flow for this claim type:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Claim received] --> B{Emergency admission?}
  B -- No --> C{Amount above SGD 3,000?}
  B -- Yes --> D[Attach ED note]
  C -- Yes --> E[Pre-authorisation form required]
  C -- No --> F[Itemised bill only]
  E --> G[Routine review]
  F --> G
  D --> G
```

The cataract claim follows the **No, Yes** path, so the form is required.
